Nature and science facts about rhinoceros beetles

The rhinoceros beetle is known for the tough horn on its head and thorax (mostly on males). It uses this horn to lift and push away other males in contests over a good spot where tree sap flows. It's so strong for its body size that it's called the "strongman." It goes through a complete transformation (egg → larva → pupa → adult), and the larva grows plump inside rotting wood and leaf-mold soil.

Great points to observe together

Point out things like the horn (on males), the pushing contests (lifting), the "strongman" strength, and the larva in leaf-mold soil. Talking about "What does it do with its horn?" together is a great idea.

Parent guide — how to nurture curiosity

Compare a stag beetle (pincers) and a rhinoceros beetle (horn) to spot the difference in their weapons. Talking about how "it makes such great strength from such a small body (a strongman)" makes it even more exciting.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What does a rhinoceros beetle use its horn for?
A. It uses it in contests over sap spots to lift and push away other males. Mostly males have one.

Q. Why is it called the strongman?
A. Because it's incredibly strong for its body size. It can easily push things heavier than itself.

Q. How can we observe them at home?
A. Compare its weapon with a stag beetle's (pincers), and talk about the larva in leaf-mold soil.
